name: Meridian Munitions MM-4 'Breadwinner'
description:
Meridian Munitions designed the MM-4 specifically for the freelancer market — operators who need corporate-grade reliability without corporate-grade prices or corporate-grade surveillance. The Breadwinner chambers 6mm caseless in a bullpup configuration that keeps the barrel length at 450mm while maintaining an overall length under 700mm. A basic BCI interface provides aim-assist without the full neural handshake that premium weapons demand.

The MM-4's defining feature is its open-architecture accessory rail system, which accepts attachments from any manufacturer rather than locking users into a proprietary ecosystem. This makes it the preferred platform for operators who mix and match equipment from multiple sources. Meridian even publishes the rail specifications openly, encouraging third-party development.

At Φ2,800 for a standard unit, the Breadwinner occupies the sweet spot between the disposable KPA-15 and premium corporate rifles. It rewards skilled marksmanship without demanding neural augmentation, making it popular among operators who keep their BCI integration minimal.
specifications:
caliber: 6mm caseless
effective_range: 450m
rate_of_fire: 720 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 35 rounds
weight: 3.0 kg
tactical_use: The MM-4 is a workhorse for independent operators. Its compact bullpup layout excels in vehicle operations and urban environments where overall length matters. The open accessory system means operators can configure the weapon for any mission profile without buying into a single manufacturer's ecosystem. The basic BCI aim-assist provides a meaningful accuracy improvement without requiring deep neural integration.
cultural_context: The Breadwinner's name is literal — it is the tool that puts food on the table for thousands of freelance operators across GLMZ. Meridian Munitions has cultivated a reputation as the arms manufacturer that respects operator independence, and the MM-4 embodies that ethos. In freelancer bars and safe houses, the Breadwinner is the default rifle, as common and unremarkable as a work tool should be.
story_hooks: Meridian Munitions is being pressured by Arcturus to close their open-architecture specs. If they comply, thousands of freelancers lose their equipment ecosystem overnight.
A modified Breadwinner recovered from an assassination has aftermarket parts from six different manufacturers — tracing the weapon means tracing six separate supply chains.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular bullpup assault rifle with a distinctly modular aesthetic. The weapon presents a forward-heavy silhouette with prominent accessory rails dominating the upper receiver and sides. Its purposeful, utilitarian design reads as a tool built for professionals who value flexibility over fashion.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 685mm | Barrel length: 450mm | Height (with picatinny rail): 95mm | Width: 65mm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 3.0kg. The weight distribution favors the front end due to the caseless mechanism, creating a naturally steadied aim platform. Feels substantial without being burdensome—designed for extended operational periods.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer receiver with steel barrel assembly and hybrid aluminum/steel accessory rail framework. The bullpup layout concentrates harder materials toward the firing mechanism.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel rail sections. Strategic areas show anodized gunmetal gray where materials meet. Deliberately subdued—designed for environments where tactical black might be too conspicuous.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: dark charcoal gray with gunmetal steel accents. Secondary: Φ green data-port indicators around the BCI interface housing. Minimal branding presence.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with slight ribbing for positive purchase even through gloved hands. The magazine well features aggressive forward serrations. Rail surfaces maintain a fine-tooth machining pattern to reduce reflection.
distinctive_features: Integrated BCI interface module mounted on the left side of the receiver—visible as a small hexagonal data port with soft Φ-green LED indicator
Open-standard picatinny rails across upper receiver, both sides, and bottom—visually emphasizes the modular architecture
Caseless ammunition feed system visible through translucent magazine with round count markings
Tactical/accessory picatinny rail sections show manufacturing hash marks and tolerance stamps
Forward assist charging handle positioned for left-hand manipulation in bullpup configuration
Vented heat shroud along the barrel—small parallel slots suggest efficient thermal management
Magazine catch positioned for ambidextrous reload operation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS etched in small caps across the upper receiver just forward of the charging handle. Small mm-4 designator stamped below. Serial plate mounted on lower receiver rear. Φ2,800 price point sometimes laser-engraved inside magazine well by dealers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained but not pristine. Polymer shows light scuff marks from equipment contact. Rails may display minor wear from accessory changes. BCI interface usually protected with a quick-release dust cover. Well-kept operators maintain this weapon—it responds to care with reliability.
